purpose: Versioned source register for research baselines in cloth simulation, robotic garment manipulation, textile sorting and sewing. This manifest does not declare any dataset ingested or authorize redistribution. This revision adds OpenTextile-NIR, two inverse-design research comparators, a design-sorting mismatch study and a 2026 critical fabric-design review. Reported percentages/metrics are source-specific and must not be treated as universal or reproduced Luminous results. This revision adds apparel scheduling comparators spanning dual-resource MIP/CP/heuristics, textile steam-aware multi-objective RL, source-load coordination, multi-line flow shops and human-centered scheduling. Published case results are scope-specific and are not a common leaderboard. This revision adds ASTM D6673-10 pattern interchange, the Knitout v0.6 machine-independent knitting instruction format and an open parametric sweater reference generator. These formats cover different layers and must not be conflated as a complete garment digital thread. This revision adds human-AI sustainable fashion co-design, sketch-to-parametric garment generation, spatially varying ease/pattern extraction, controllable fashion diffusion and multimodal sketch/text-to-pattern sources. These are distinct levels of the workflow; image generation, editable pattern generation, 3D fit evaluation and physical product qualification must not be conflated. This revision adds textile-reinforced concrete and digital construction sources: process classification, hybrid textile/SHCC placement, robotic rebar insertion/grouting, in-process mesh placement, robotic steel reinforcement/welding and textile-waste cementitious composites. These are structural-material benchmarks, distinct from apparel qualification. Revision r7 adds the textile pre-processing review, NIR contamination and elastane challenges, and industrial/reuse-flow evidence for polyester-cotton and stretch-textile recovery. Identification, physical separation, material output and downstream acceptance remain separate evaluation stages. Revision r8 explicitly records ASTM D6673-10 as withdrawn in 2019 (legacy compatibility only), adds the NIST STEP/EXPRESS apparel-pattern information-model precedent, and separates Knitout syntax from backend/machine execution support.
